Subject: Discovery Recap & PoC plan — FastRetail integration

Hi Emily / Raj —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery to make sure we’re aligned and to confirm next steps for a short PoC: 

Pain points you shared
- Search relevance & product discovery underperforming for long-tail SKUs.
- Current embedding pipeline (in-house TF embeddings) has high inference cost and latency at scale.
- Need deterministic, explainable scoring for merchandising rules (so buyers can trust automated suggestions).

Current stack
- Backend: Node.js microservices on AWS ECS
- Vector store: Pinecone (evaluation cluster) + Postgres for metadata
- Frontend: React storefront with SSR
- Auth/analytics: FastRetail internal SSO + Segment

Success criteria for PoC (agreed)
1) 10–15% lift in click-through-rate on surfaced recommendations (A/B against current model)
2) Avg tail-query latency < 200ms p50 for embedding+search path
3) Integration that preserves existing merchandising rules (explainable score fields)

Proposed PoC scope & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): Share PoC plan and access requirements — attachments included (FastRetail_PoC-plan-vanessa-v1.docx).
- Week 1: SDK integration (Node.js) + small batch of sample SKUs (10k) — endpoint tests and smoke evaluations.
- Week 2: Deploy test route behind feature flag, run A/B for 1 week on 5% traffic.
- Week 3: Evaluate metrics, collect qualitative feedback, decide expansion.

Owners
- Redwood: Vanessa (AM) — project lead / timeline, Ben (SE) — integration & performance tuning, Marissa (CS) — onboarding support and eval hooks.
- FastRetail: Emily (Product), Raj (Engineering) — infra & deployment owner.

Technical notes / compatibility
- SDKs: We recommend using redwood-js (Node) or redwood-py (Python). For your stack, Node SDK will require minor changes to your existing service (we provide an Express example).
- API compatibility: Standard REST + streaming option for recommendations; supports existing embedding formats and custom metadata.
- Rate limits & quotas: For the PoC we can temporarily raise throughput to 100 rps on the test route.

Next steps (action items)
- Emily/Raj: Share sample SKU export (+ schema) and a non-prod AWS role for test deployment by end of day Fri.
- Vanessa: Send final PoC doc + initial test route config (attached).
- Ben/Marissa: Schedule a 30-min integration call for next Tue to walkthrough SDK and test harness.

I attached a short PoC plan and our API playbook for your infra team. Let me know if anything above needs correction.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Hi Emily / Vanessa — thanks for the details. A couple technical confirmations ahead of Tue’s integration call: 

1) Node SDK & serverless: The redwood-js SDK supports both server and serverless runtimes (Lambda / Vercel). For SSR pages we recommend calling Redwood from an API route (server-side) rather than the edge runtime to preserve KV cache semantics and consistent latency. If you want edge inference we can supply a reduced model config for lower memory.

2) Embedding format: We accept float32 embeddings or quantized uint8 depending on your pipeline. If you prefer to continue with your TF pipeline we can accept the embeddings as-is and host the reranking/search. Alternately, we can host the embedding step; for PoC we suggest you provide your existing embeddings so we can isolate search/regression effects.

3) Throughput: We can provision 100 rps during PoC. For production sizing (if roll-forward) we’ll need a short load profile; I’ll prepare a simple script you can run for 30 minutes to collect realistic request traces.

4) Explainability: We’ll surface score breakdowns (semantic score, merchandising boost, rule penalties) in the response JSON so your UI team can show contributors which factors influenced the result.

I’ve attached the API playbook with example payloads and test harness commands. We’ll walk through these examples on Tue.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
